title: Customer Residency Onboarding and SLA Alignment Playbook
body:
Purpose
This is a customer-facing onboarding playbook and internal runbook for aligning residency preferences, SLA commitments, and fallback behavior for Private/Dedicated customers. It collects the minimal set of legal/ops/engineering checks we need to get a customer from contract signature to production residency enforcement and monitoring.

Context and scope
- Scope: onboarding for customers choosing region pinning (single region or geo-merged) and wanting clear SLAs + fallback policies. Covers: contract language to request, engineering pin configuration, customer acceptance tests (CATs), telemetry to capture, and communications templates.
- Not scope: deep legal negotiation (hand off to legal), physical on-prem hardware procurement.

High-level goals
1) Ensure the customer has a documented residency decision and corresponding SLA language in their contract.
2) Validate the platform enforces pinning for 99.9% of requests (operational target we translate into test acceptance criteria).
3) Provide a transparent fallback policy for cross-region spillover and emergency routing.
4) Produce a repeatable verification plan for the customer and internal SRE/AE teams.

Onboarding checkpoints (owner: Solutions Eng / Customer Success)
- Contract check (Day 0): Confirm contract includes the chosen residency option: REGION_PIN = [region-id e.g. eu-west1] or MULTI_REGION = [list]. Include simple SLA snippet recommending: "Residency enforcement target 99.9% of API requests; fallback may route to approved secondary region under capacity/emergency events; customer will be notified via email and dashboard incident."
- Security & KMS check (Day 1): Confirm customer KMS integration and region-bound key material where required. Ticket template: KMS|Customer|Region|Status.
- Network/VPC check (Day 2): Validate VPC peering, firewall rules, and allowed egress policies for pinned region.
- Configuration check (Day 3): Apply region pin config in control plane (see sample below).
- Verification window (Day 4–7): Run acceptance tests (see CATs) and produce verification report.

Sample control-plane snippet (for handoff to infra team)
- Customer ID: CUST-2021-139
- Residency.mode = "pin"
- Residency.primary_region = "eu-west1"
- Residency.secondary_regions = ["eu-central1"] // optional, used only for defined fallback windows
- Residency.enforcement_policy = "strict-with-notify" // values: strict, allow-fallback, best-effort
- Notification.email = "ops@customer.com"

Customer Acceptance Tests (CATs) – run by SE with customer
1) Pin enforcement basic test
   - Precondition: config applied and propagated to all control plane members
   - Test: issue 1,000 short requests from a test client with country=DE geo header and customer api-key pinned to eu-west1
   - Success: >= 999 requests served from nodes in eu-west1 (99.9%); trace IDs show region tag eu-west1.
2) Cross-region request detection
   - Test: simulate traffic where source IP resolves to an IP outside EU. Confirm request is rejected/blocked or routed per policy.
   - Success: routing decision recorded and customer notified if routed elsewhere.
3) Fallback during capacity event
   - Test: run synthetic load while artificially draining 30% capacity in eu-west1 (simulated). Verify spillover path to eu-central1 only if secondary_regions configured and only when enforcement_policy==allow-fallback.
   - Success: fallback percentage <= configured threshold and all fallback events are logged with reason.
4) End-to-end telemetry validation
   - Test: verify traces include: customer_id, region_tag, enforcement_decision, fallback_reason (if any). Confirm logs emitted to the customer dashboard and to audit bucket.
   - Success: All fields present for sample traces.

Acceptance criteria (SRE measurable)
- Enforcement accuracy: >= 99.9% of requests for pinned customers are served from pinned region in normal ops.
- Visibility: 100% of enforcement decisions have trace logs with region tags and enforcement status.
- Notification: Customer gets automated email or dashboard incident for any spillover/fallback event within 15 minutes of detection.
- Remediation Time objective (RTO): For faults causing cross-region failover, engineering rollback or mitigation plan initiated within 30 minutes.

Telemetry and audit events to capture
- residency.enforcement_check (tags: customer_id, request_id, observed_region, intended_region, decision, node_id)
- residency.fallback_event (tags: customer_id, request_count, fallback_region, reason_code)
- residency.config_change (tags: who, old_value, new_value, timestamp)
- residency.kms_bind (tags: customer_id, key_id, region)

SLA / contract language suggestions (for AM/Legal to copy)
- Residency enforcement: "Provider will make reasonable commercial efforts to ensure that service requests for Customer data are processed in the Customer-specified region(s) as set forth in Exhibit A. Provider's target enforcement rate for pinned regions is 99.9% during normal operations. This target excludes events resulting from force majeure, customer misconfiguration, or scheduled maintenance."
- Fallback policy: "In the event of capacity constraints, networking partition, or other exceptional circumstances, Provider may route requests to pre-authorized secondary region(s). Provider will notify Customer within 15 minutes of such routing and publish a post-incident summary."
- Audit rights: "Customer may request up to one residency enforcement audit per 12-month period; Provider will provide trace excerpts and aggregate statistics subject to nondisclosure constraints."

Communications templates
1) Initial onboarding email (to customer ops)
   Subject: Residency onboarding next steps — [Customer]
   Body: Hi [Name], next week we'll: (1) apply the residency pin to eu-west1, (2) validate KMS binding, (3) run acceptance tests. Please provide a contact for incident notifications and any additional regions you want listed as secondary.
2) Fallback notification (automated)
   Subject: Residency fallback event — [Customer] — eu-west1 -> eu-central1
   Body: We detected a capacity-driven spillover affecting ~12% of requests for [duration]. Fallback reason: capacity shortfall due to node maintenance. Actions: autoscale triggered, additional capacity requested, postmortem planned.

Runbook for on-call (abridged)
- Detect: Alert where residency.fallback_event rate > 0.5% sustained over 5 minutes for pinned customers.
- Triage: Confirm reason (capacity, network partition, KMS failure). Check recent config changes.
- Mitigate: If capacity, trigger dedicated scaling path or enable emergency burst to secondary region per contract. If KMS, roll to fallback keys (with legal approval).
- Communicate: Post incident to customer channel, create PSR (post-stage report).

Edge cases and operator notes
- Partial-population pin: Some customers ask for pin by customer_id but not admin events (e.g., audit logs). Capture this in the config and ensure logs are explicitly marked as non-customer-data.
- Mixed-hosting: If a customer uses both Hosted and Private, ensure route maps include tenancy mapping and clearly document which product serves which traffic.
- Regulatory freeze: When legal requests a freeze on config changes, tag residency.config_change tickets with "regulatory-freeze" and route to legal+secops approval steps.

Templates and tickets
- Jira template: RESIDENCY-ONBOARD-TEMPLATE
  Summary: Onboard residency for [Customer] -> primary: [region]
  Description: list of required items (contract clause, KMS, VPC setup, control-plane config, CATs result), owners and dates.

Open questions (to resolve before finalizing with customer)
- Does the customer want signed authorization for fallback to a specific set of secondary regions? (answers change our config fields)
- Are audit logs acceptable in an alternate region if they are encrypted end-to-end and access-controlled?
- Will the customer require per-request geo-assertion headers for regulatory auditing?

Next steps (for SE/AE)
1) Schedule 60-minute residency kickoff with customer and SRE. Bring this playbook.
2) Fill the onboarding Jira template and attach KMS/VPC artifacts.
3) Run CATs and produce verification report; if acceptance criteria unmet, open follow-up engineering tickets and negotiate temporary mitigation with customer.

Appendix: quick checklist (copyable)
- [ ] Contract residency clause present and countersigned
- [ ] AE/SE customer contact for ops provided
- [ ] KMS binding verified in chosen region
- [ ] VPC/network validated for region egress patterns
- [ ] Control-plane pin config applied and propagated
- [ ] CATs executed and report uploaded
- [ ] Dashboard telemetry validated and alert configured

End of playbook.

Notes: This doc is intended for incremental improvement; if field teams run into repeated gaps, capture them as issues under the RESIDENCY_ONBOARD backlog tag.
